name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
principle: The product accepts uploaded files with dangerous types and stores or transfers them where the environment may automatically process them. If an uploaded script, markup, or executable handler type is reachable, attackers can execute code or trigger client-side attacks.
detection_signals: Java MultipartFile.transferTo(new File(webRoot, file.getOriginalFilename())) without allowlist extension check
Java Servlet Part.write(part.getSubmittedFileName()) using submitted filename
C/C++ multipart handler writes Content-Disposition filename directly with fopen/open/FileWriter equivalent
validation checks only request Content-Type, Part.getContentType(), or $_FILES[..]['type']
extension filtering uses denylist such as !endsWith(".php") instead of allowlist
uploaded files saved under web document root such as /var/www, htdocs, public, static, or wwwroot
negative_signals: server generates filename with UUID/random ID and fixed safe extension
case-insensitive allowlist such as .jpg/.png/.pdf enforced on server side
code rejects filenames with multiple extensions or path separators before storage
uploaded bytes stored outside web document root and served only through a controlled download endpoint
file type validation combines extension allowlist with magic-byte/content parser verification
web server configuration disables script execution in upload directory
false_defense_traps: HTML input accept attribute or JavaScript-only file validation
trusting MIME type from Content-Type or multipart part header
denylisting dangerous extensions while allowing unknown extensions
case-sensitive extension checks on case-insensitive file systems
checking only the last extension and allowing filename.php.gif
magic-byte checks alone; formats can contain executable comments or active content
verification_focus: Can an attacker upload a file with a server-processed or client-active type and make the application or environment process it?

consequence_chains.trigger: uploaded .html/.svg file is served to other users as active content
uploaded .php/.jsp/.asp file is stored in an executable web path

patch_principle: Use a strict server-side allowlist of business-required file types and reject all others.
Generate a new unique filename and safe fixed extension; never use the user-supplied filename for storage.
Store uploads outside the web document root or disable handler/script execution in the upload directory.
Require a single normalized extension and perform case-insensitive checks.
Validate content with a parser or magic-byte check as a secondary control, not the only control.
